subject: Post-demo recap: bespoke eval / data contract for Pulsewell
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Roth <maya.roth@pulsewellhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: bespoke eval / data contract for Pulsewell

Hi Maya — great to meet today, and thanks for walking us through the sample use cases and the clinician workflow. Per our demo and the follow-up discussion, summary + immediate next steps below so we stay aligned.

Key asks you outlined
- Prioritise accuracy on short diagnostic summaries and appropriate triage recommendations (primary metric: macro F1 for label-level classification; secondary: generation precision measured by inferred-span matching).
- Limit latency to <350ms p50 for interactive assistant flows; batch jobs can run asynchronously.
- Data handling requirements: redaction + hashed IDs, SOC2 audit readiness for hosting.

Redwood recommended starting stack (initial run)- Model shortlist (we'll run parallel evals):
  - Llama-2-70b-chat (fp16) — expected best quality baseline
  - Llama-2-13b-chat (8-bit quant) — cost/latency tradeoff candidate
  - ReduLite-7B-QR — low-cost baseline for throughput-sensitive endpoints

Benchmarks & assets- Prompt bank + scoring rubric (attached: redwood_eval_template_v2.xlsx)
- Example benchmark runner: https://console.redwood.ai/jobs/exec-7321
- Sample prompt subsets we'll use: triage_prompt_set_v1 (clinical triage), summary_prompt_set_v2 (concise diagnostic summaries) — included in the Drive link below.

Dataset/data contract for evals (what we need from you)- Format: CSV UTF-8 with header row, one example per row. Required columns: sample_id, clinician_note, structured_context (JSON string), gold_label(s) (comma separated), expected_summary (optional).
- Max tokens: provide raw clinician_note up to 4,000 chars. If longer, include truncated_version and full_text_link.
- PII: replace PHI with [REDACTED] or supply a redaction flag column. See attached pii_redaction_guidelines.pdf.
- Size: for reliable signal, request ~2,000 scored examples split across core workflows (triage, diagnosis summary, coding suggestion). If not possible, send the largest representative sample you have and we'll stratify.

Scoring criteria (initial plan)
- Classification (triage labels): macro F1, per-class precision/recall, confusion matrix.
- Summarization: ROUGE-L and a human-annotated precision score (exact-match span scoring for key clinical facts).
- Regression monitoring: we'll run pre/post model-change checks on the same prompt set and surface any statistically significant drops (p<0.05) in macro F1 or >5 point drop in human-precision.

Operational notes for running on Redwood- We can run the benchmark on Hosted Redwood for quick turnaround (~48–72 hrs for a 2k example run) or on Dedicated capacity for larger repeatable runs. For initial runs we recommend Hosted with a pinned model snapshot.
- Tokenization note: keep prompts and expected outputs in UTF-8; we'll canonicalize whitespace and normalize numeric tokens for fair scoring.
- Artifacts: we'll share a results CSV + per-example deltas + a scoring notebook.

Next steps (action items)
1) Pulsewell: share sample dataset + confirm redaction approach (Maya) — target Tue 5/11
2) Redwood: ingest sample, run smoke-run, and share quick results + adjusted rubric (Ben/Priyom) — target Fri 5/14
3) Schedule a 30-min rubric alignment session post-smoke run (invite from me)

Attachments: redwood_eval_template_v2.xlsx, pii_redaction_guidelines.pdf
Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cPulsewellEval

Thanks again — looking forward to getting the eval pipeline running.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-2198

From: Maya Roth <maya.roth@pulsewellhealth.com>

Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@pulsewellhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: bespoke eval / data contract for Pulsewell

Vanessa — thanks for the summary and the template. A few quick confirmations:

- We'll deliver an initial batch of ~1,200 examples (mix of triage + summary) by Tue 5/11. I've attached a small sample (pulsewell_sample_batch_20260509.csv) so you can validate the ingestion schema.
- For PII we will remove direct identifiers per the guidelines, but we need your team to confirm the redaction approach is acceptable for scoring (we prefer [REDACTED] placeholder).
- Regulatory Q: can the Hosted runs be done in a SOC2-compliant instance? Procurement will ask — I can loop them after your confirmation.

Two asks from our side:
1) For the summarization metric, can you include a precision-on-facts metric (we have internal clinicians who will spot-check)?
2) Please include an estimated cost for the full 2k-run across your three model candidates so we can prepare the procurement case.

Attaching: pulsewell_sample_batch_20260509.csv (1,000 rows sample for schema check).

Best,
Maya
Sr Product Manager — Clinical AI
Pulsewell Health
maya.roth@pulsewellhealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo recap: bespoke eval / data contract for Pulsewell — technical notes

Vanessa / Priyom — quick internal follow-up based on Maya's sample and the rubric:

Notes on ingestion:
- The sample CSV looks good; column names in the template map cleanly. Two things to validate with Pulsewell: (a) structured_context JSON must be consistent (we will require a schema example), (b) any non-ascii characters in notes should be normalized.

Scoring/rubric suggestions (proposal)
1) Classification (triage): macro F1 reported + per-class support. Also flag low-support classes (<25 examples) to avoid noisy estimates.
2) Summarization: proposed two-stage score: automated ROUGE-L + clinical-fact-precision. For fact precision we'll run an automated entity overlap (key-entities extracted via medical NER) then sample 200 summaries for clinician human precision scoring.
3) Regression guardrails: define a "blame window" — if model A drops >5% macro F1 vs baseline, we trigger manual review and rollback. Also produce per-prompt delta waterfall so customer sees which prompts regress most.

Execution plan on Redwood- Hosted quick-run: we can spin up the eval job using the console job exec-7321; expected runtime for 1.2k examples across three models ~6–10 hours (parallel). Cost estimate (very rough):
  - Llama-2-70b: $1,400
  - Llama-2-13b (8-bit): $320
  - ReduLite-7B: $85
We should produce a more precise estimate after we confirm sequence-length distribution.

Tech flags for Priyom to check before ingest:
- Tokenization: ensure consistent token counts by normalizing whitespace and canonicalizing punctuation.
- Batch handling: cap request batch size to 8 for 70b to keep p50 latency under 350ms in Hosted smoke runs.
- Caching: enable prefix KV cache for repeated prompts (where appropriate) to reduce run cost for iterative scoring.

I'll draft the scoring worksheet updates and attach them to the Drive folder.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Staff Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: bespoke eval / data contract for Pulsewell

Maya — thanks for the sample, that helps a lot. Quick replies inline and next steps: 

- Redaction: [REDACTED] placeholder is fine — we will treat that token as a canonical redaction and not penalize during scoring. We'll note this in the scoring workbook.
- SOC2: Hosted runs will be executed in our SOC2-compliant environment for any customer-provided data; I'll include SOC2 attestation and the compliance contact in the next email for procurement.
- Fact-precision: yes — Ben's two-stage approach is what we'll run. Automated signals + a clinician spot-check. We'll include the human spot-check plan in the rubric and estimate the effort (200 samples x clinician rate).

Cost estimate: Ben's back-of-envelope numbers above are a good starting point. We'll produce a formal cost sheet after we inspect the full 1.2k payload and token distribution.

Scheduling
- I scheduled a 30-min rubric alignment on Thu 5/13 at 10:00 AM PT — invite coming now.
- Action items recap:
   * Pulsewell: upload the full sample CSV to Drive and confirm redaction approach (Maya) — due Tue 5/11 EOD
   * Redwood: smoke-run + preliminary scoring worksheet + cost estimate (Ben/Priyom) — due Fri 5/14
